idea: Themed weeks, School and health day: written from the source, then corrected by two independent editors before voicing.
description: In Uttarakhand, 83.2% of babies were born in a health facility in the 2019-21 family health survey and 88.9% in the 2023-24 survey: up 5.7 points, against India's 2.0 (88.6% to 90.6%).

Births outside a facility went from about 17 to 11 per 100, a third fewer. The base is babies born in the five years before each survey; public and private facilities both count. Survey estimates: small gaps are not differences. The survey shows how many, not why.
source: International Institute for Population Sciences, National Family Health Survey: NFHS-6 (2023-24) state fact sheets, which also print the NFHS-5 (2019-21) figure. Share of babies born in the five years before each survey who were born in a health facility, public or private. 34 states and UTs with a figure in both surveys; Lakshadweep (small sample) is not ranked and Manipur has no figure in the sheets used. Survey estimates.
